about: Gran Enemigo is the top blend from El Enemigo, the winery Alejandro Vigil, chief winemaker of Catena Zapata, founded in 2008 with Adrianna Catena, historian and youngest daughter of Nicolás Catena. When the project began, this was the only Gran Enemigo; it has since become the flagship of a family of single-vineyard wines. The name reflects the founders’ motto, “we are our own worst enemy”, a reminder that the hardest battles are with oneself.

Gran Enemigo is a Bordeaux-style blend led by Malbec, Argentina’s adopted grape. In 2020 half the wine is Malbec, with Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and a dash of Petit Verdot. The fruit comes from Gualtallary, about 1,470 metres up in the Uco Valley. Malbec and Cabernet Franc grow on rocky, calcareous soils, while the other varieties grow on deeper sandy ground. After fermentation and long maceration, the wine ages about fifteen months in a century-old foudre rather than new barrels, so it keeps its freshness and chalky grip.

Wine Advocate gave the 2020 95 points and suggested it may be the finest vintage of Gran Enemigo yet; Descorchados also rated it 95. Tasting notes from the trade describe cocoa, red fruit and orange peel over herbal, minty and spicy tones, with fresh acidity and a dry, chalky finish. It is built for the cellar, with a drinking window that importers place into the early to mid 2030s.
facts: 50% Malbec, 20% Cabernet Franc, 20% Cabernet Sauvignon, 5% Merlot, 5% Petit Verdot
